title: A Flood Story on a Clay Tablet
objective: After this level you can explain how the flood story in Gilgamesh was recognized in 1872 and how it parallels the flood in Genesis.
summary: In 1872 George Smith read a flood story on the 11th tablet of Gilgamesh. Like Noah, Utnapishtim builds a boat, saves animals and sends out birds, but the reasons and endings differ.

cards.headline: In 1872, a man read a broken clay tablet and started to undress.
cards.body: According to a later account, George Smith of the British Museum jumped up and rushed about the room in great excitement, then began taking off his clothes. What could an old tablet say to do that to a person?

cards.headline: A ship, a mountain, a dove
cards.body: Smith had been apprenticed to a banknote engraver at 14, then taught himself to read cuneiform. On one tablet, as he later wrote, his eye caught a ship resting on a mountain, then a dove sent out that found no resting place and came back. It sounded like Noah's flood in Genesis. It was on the 11th tablet of the 12-tablet Epic of Gilgamesh.

items.label: Gilgamesh
points: A god has Utnapishtim build a boat
The boat grounds on Mount Nimush
He sends out a dove, a swallow and a raven

items.label: Genesis
points: God tells Noah to build an ark
Male and female of every animal
The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
Noah sends out a raven and a dove

cards.headline: Same shape, different meaning
cards.body: Scholars see Babylonian flood traditions as the source of features of the biblical story, such as building and stocking the ark and the waters going down. But the two tell different stories. In the Babylonian flood, the gods disagree; in Genesis, the flood answers human wrongdoing. And the endings split: Utnapishtim joins the immortal gods, while Noah's family is sent to start history again.

cards.fact: A newspaper paid for a treasure hunt.
cards.context: Smith presented his find to the Society of Biblical Archaeology in 1872, with Prime Minister Gladstone in the audience. The Daily Telegraph then paid for an expedition to Nineveh. In May 1873, digging there, Smith found a fragment he believed completed the flood account.

cards.headline: The flood tablet: deciphered
learned: 1872: George Smith reads the flood tablet
Boat, animals, mountain, birds: shared with Genesis

questions.prompt: In 1872, George Smith recognized _____ on a clay tablet.

options.label: the oldest known world map
options.rationale: He was reading a story, not a map.

options.label: a list of Ashurbanipal's taxes
options.rationale: The tablet told of a ship, a mountain and a dove.

options.label: the first law code
options.rationale: It was part of the Epic of Gilgamesh.

questions.explanation: Smith spotted a ship resting on a mountain and a dove sent out: a flood story on the 11th tablet of Gilgamesh.

questions.prompt: The Babylonian and Genesis floods share a shape. Where do they most clearly differ?

options.label: Only the Babylonian story sends out birds
options.rationale: Noah sends a raven and a dove.

options.label: Why the flood comes: a quarrel among gods, or human wrongdoing
Only Genesis has the boat come to rest on a mountain

questions.explanation: In the Babylonian story the flood comes from a disagreement among the gods; in Genesis it answers human wrongdoing.

questions.prompt: Level 3: Gilgamesh sought Utnapishtim to learn how to escape death. What does the flood story say about Utnapishtim's own fate?

options.label: He is made immortal after the flood
He becomes king of Uruk
options.rationale: Gilgamesh is the king of Uruk.

options.label: He is sent to start human history again

questions.explanation: After the flood, Utnapishtim and his wife join the immortal gods, which is why Gilgamesh hoped he knew the secret.
